diagnosis.cause: This is a caused failure in the repository's hosted apt-timeout self-test: on the pinned candidate's ubuntu-26.04.1 environment, both timeout assertions return 137 instead of the test's required status-124 diagnostic, and the test does not currently expose the timeout command's resolved binary/argv. The self-test remains incompatible with or incorrectly invoking the hosted timeout implementation; the five external parser errors are evidence, but their emitting call is not yet identified.

failure_record.job: Code Style / Fast deterministic checks (job 140074731468), on ubuntu-26.04.1 image 20261116.202.1
failure_record.log_evidence: Exact-head replacement run https://github.com/10krco/ironclaw/actions/runs/45867664832 failed both apt hang cases: `FAIL: update hang: output missing 'timed out'`, `apt-get update failed with exit 137 (attempt 1/2)` and `(attempt 2/2)`; install has the corresponding missing timeout message and two exit-137 failures. The log also emits five `timeout` parser errors saying required `<duration>` and `<command>` were not provided, outside the installer output redirected to the test sandbox. Current test resets PATH to `$sandbox:/usr/bin:/bin`; installer invokes `sudo env ... timeout --signal=INT --kill-after=30s 2s apt-get ...`; fake sudo is `exec "$@"`; fake hanging apt uses `exec sleep 120`. The previous exec-sleep change did not fix the hosted run. The parser-error source/argv remains unproven.
